item.title: Abbott to Pay $670 Million to Settle Some Preterm Infant Formula Cases
item.description: Abbott said on Thursday it reached a $670 million settlement to partially resolve the ongoing litigation over alleged harms linked to its specialty formulas for preterm infants. The settlement was agreed to by three law firms representing about 2,000 people with claims against Abbott, including one Illinois mother who won a $495 million judgment in 2024 after a jury concluded that Abbott’s formula caused her daughter to develop necrotizing enterocolitis, a dangerous bowel disease. Abbott did not admit liability in Thursday’s settlement, saying it remains confident in the safety of its infant formula products.

item.title: 5 Interesting Startup Deals You May Have Missed: AI For Everything From Recycling To Breathing To Winning Construction Bids
item.description: This is a monthly column that runs down five interesting startup funding deals that may have flown under the radar. This month’s installment of this column is all AI, though applications for the technology range widely, from two startups that apply AI to trash or recycling, to another that promises to help people breathe and sleep better, to a company that says its AI can help architects and builders spot commercial projects before they’re even announced. For decades, the recycling industry has relied on sampling and educated guesses to understand what moves through its facilities.

item.title: Bermuda reinsurers and sidecars drive US life insurance sector’s expansion: ALIRT
item.description: A recent report from ALIRT Insurance Research suggests that steady growth amongst Bermuda reinsurers and sidecars are responsible for a significant portion of the U.S. life insurance sector’s expansion in recent years. As previously highlighted, ALIRT also identified continued growth in newly established Bermuda reinsurers and sidecar structures.

item.title: RenRe third-party capital ILS assets managed hit $8.54bn at H1 2026, up 5.5% in last year
item.description: RenaissanceRe Capital Partners, the specialist third-party capital management division of the reinsurer, lifted its partnering investor capital managed across joint-venture reinsurance and insurance-linked securities strategies by around 5.5% over the last year, to end June 2026 with $8.54 billion of assets under management. Third-party investor capital across the RenaissanceRe Capital Partners managed joint-ventures and ILS funds ended June 2025 at $8.09 billion, but rose through the end of last year to the $9.08 billion record-high. DaVinci Re had third-party AUM of $3.69 billion across its equity and debt as of the mid-year 2026, up from $3.35 billion at January 1st, while Vermeer Re had $1.89 billion of assets at June 30th, slightly higher than the Jan 1st $1.77 billion.

item.title: Malaysian Re drives 76.3% of MNRB’s profit after tax in Q1 FY’27
item.description: MNRB Holdings Berhad’s wholly owned subsidiary, Malaysian Reinsurance Berhad (Malaysian Re), reported profit after tax of RM140.2 million for the first quarter of the financial year ending 31 March 2027, up 25.1% year over year from RM112.1 million and contributing 76.3% of the group’s overall profit after tax. Malaysian Re’s profit after tax growth was driven by stable insurance/takaful service results and improved investment results, underpinned by higher unrealised foreign exchange gains. Their combined profit after tax increased 23.8% to RM29.6 million from RM23.9 million in Q1 FY2026, driven by higher wakalah income from both the family and general business portfolios.

item.title: Skyward Group sets out CFO succession plan ahead of Mark Haushill’s retirement
item.description: and Apollo Group Holdings Ltd., has announced a planned change in its senior financial leadership, with current Chief Financial Officer Mark Haushill set to retire next year. Taryn McHarg, currently Chief Financial Officer of Apollo and Deputy CFO of Skyward Group, has been selected to succeed Haushill. She will assume the Skyward Group CFO role following his retirement.

item.title: P&C insurers have the opportunity to turn profitability gains into a lasting advantage: Aon
item.description: New analysis from global professional services firm Aon suggests that global property and casualty insurers are entering the next phase of the market cycle from a position of strength, creating an opportunity to turn recent profitability gains into long-term competitive advantage. Aon’s analysis has underlined five key areas for insurers to avoid as they seek to sustain profitable growth: Don’t confuse strong returns with sustainable growth; don’t defer difficult choices on where to grow; don’t miss the opportunity to make capital a strategic asset; don’t delay investments in people and technology; and don’t let AI become someone else’s advantage. The benefits of “acting now” are significant, Aon said, as stronger profitability gives insurers the flexibility to invest in underwriting, portfolio analytics, reinsurance strategy, digital capabilities and talent.

item.title: Sydney Air Traffic Controllers Warn of Grave Safety Concerns
item.description: Air traffic controllers in Sydney have warned of “grave concerns” about flight safety because of new local airspace rules, the safety regulator said, just as the number of near misses and incidents at the airport mounts. In the anonymous safety warning, the controller said more than 50 colleagues in Sydney had responded to a survey by Civil Air, the union for Australian air traffic controllers. The whistleblower said many air traffic controllers in Sydney, where they are already shorthanded, have little confidence in their ability to handle the new rules, which were introduced last month and are tied to the new Western Sydney International airport.

item.title: Rhode Spill: Summer Heat Turns Truckload of Spilled Squid Into Unappetizing Mess
item.description: A tractor-trailer rollover sent a truckload of squid spilling onto a Rhode Island roadway, leaving a stench as they sat in the road for hours in the summer heat. Local authorities have dubbed it the “Squidpocalypse of ’26.” It was a warm, sunny day in the coastal town of Narragansett when the spill happened Sunday, and Narragansett Police Capt. Ryan Prest said he was told that the scene “started to smell bad as the squid sat out in the sun for a few hours.” The fully-loaded trailer was taking the squid to a processing facility out of town when the trailer dislodged and tipped on its side as the driver was navigating a turn, spilling a “substantial portion” of its calamari cargo, the police department said in a statement.

item.title: A$385m ClearView deal: Zurich completes Australian life buy as composite insurers rebuild protection books
item.description: The post A$385m ClearView deal: Zurich completes Australian life buy as composite insurers rebuild protection books appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Zurich has completed its acquisition of ASX-listed life insurer ClearView Wealth, a move that underlines a wider strategy among global composite insurers to rebuild the life and protection books their rivals spent years dismantling. The deal cleared the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority, shareholders, and the Supreme Court of New South Wales.

item.title: General Contractor Found Not Liable for Subcontractor Employee’s Injury
item.description: A general contractor cannot be held liable for an injury of an employee of a subcontractor where the general contractor had little or no control over the subcontractor’s work or job environment. The general contractor argued it had not retained sufficient control over MBT’s work to be liable, and that Massachusetts law does not recognize a negligent hiring claim brought by a subcontractor’s employee against a general contractor. The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court this week upheld a summary judgment in favor of New York general contractor Skyway Roofing against claims of negligence and negligent hiring brought by an injured roofer who worked for one of its subcontractors.

item.title: Former NFL QB Hasselbeck on Frontier: Diagnosing CTE Disease in the Living
item.description: The hope is that it will be a small step toward a goal that has eluded doctors — diagnosing chronic traumatic encephalopathy in the living. They had my back, so in a way I’d like to have their back.” CTE puts harsh spotlight on NFL, college football A degenerative brain disease that has been linked to concussions and other head trauma common in military combat and contact sports, CTE has been diagnosed in more than 100 former NFL players, casting a pall over the United States’ most popular sports league. Matt Hasselbeck took some nasty hits to the head during his 17-year NFL career, four years at Boston College and a childhood full of sports, but the quarterback seems to have emerged from more than two decades of collisions relatively unscathed, enjoying middle adulthood with his wife and three children.

item.title: Appeals Court Revives Signature Bank Collapse Lawsuit Despite FDIC Objection
item.description: appeals court on Wednesday revived an investor lawsuit over the 2023 collapse of Signature Bank, saying the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp (FDIC) seizure of the lender did not take away shareholders’ right to sue. Circuit Court of Appeals in Manhattan rejected the FDIC’s argument that a 1989 law adopted in the wake of that decade’s savings-and-loan crisis gave the regulator sole power to pursue securities fraud claims after becoming the receiver of a failed bank. Regulators closed Signature on March 12, 2023, after worried customers withdrew several billion dollars, or about 20% of its deposits following the collapse of the larger Silicon Valley Bank two days earlier.

item.title: Adam Fox to lead Stonybrook’s international growth
item.description: Stonybrook, a global specialist investment banking and reinsurance broking firm, has announced the appointment of Adam Fox as CEO of International, a London-based role. In his new position, the executive will lead efforts to expand Stonybrook’s international platform and support the firm’s US business, especially its trading relationships with the specialist Lloyd’s marketplace. Commenting on his appointment Fox said: “Having spent my career working across insurance, reinsurance and capital markets, I see a significant opportunity to help Stonybrook expand its international platform and connect clients with differentiated capital and risk solutions.

item.title: Clearwater expands underwriting platform into Crisis Management market
item.description: Clearwater Underwriting, a specialty underwriting business focused on marine risks, has entered the Crisis Management market with the appointment of Tim Strong as Managing Director, Crisis Management. Strong commented: “I’m delighted to have joined Clearwater Underwriting at such an exciting stage in the company’s trajectory, and I’m looking forward to building out its Crisis Management portfolio. Clearwater aims to meet this demand with a technology-enabled, disciplined underwriting approach, while building a broader Crisis Management capability over time.

item.title: AM Best upgrades Kinsale’s Issuer Credit Ratings
item.description: AM Best has upgraded Kinsale Insurance Company’s Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating (Long-Term ICR) to “a+” (Excellent) from “a” (Excellent) and affirmed its Financial Strength Rating (FSR) of A (Excellent). The ratings are also supported by Kinsale’s risk-adjusted capitalisation at the strongest level, as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR), as well as continued organic surplus growth driven by consistent underwriting profitability and reliable net investment income. AM Best also upgraded Kinsale Capital Group, Inc.’s Long-Term ICR to “bbb+” (Good) from “bbb” (Good), with the outlook revised to stable from positive.

item.title: Snapsheet, claimtouch Integrate Contents Claims
item.description: (Image source: Snapsheet and claimtouch.) Snapsheet (Chicago) and claimtouch (New York) have launched an integration designed to bring contents claims intelligence directly into the Snapsheet Claims Platform. Snapsheet and claimtouch say the relationship is intended to bring more automation to contents claims without adding fragmentation or data inconsistencies. “Our mission is to enable adjusters to help policyholders recover faster—a commitment we share with Snapsheet.” claimtouch provides an AI-native contents claims platform for inventory collection, valuation, settlement and claim resolution.

item.title: Is Your Insurance Core System/Platform Agent-Ready?
item.description: An API-first architecture asks: “How can another application interact with my platform?” An agent-ready architecture adds: “How can an AI agent discover what my platform can do and safely use those capabilities?” Early Insurance Examples We are beginning to see versions of this architecture emerge in the insurance technology market. If I were evaluating a core insurance platform today, I would therefore add a section to the RFP called “Agent Readiness.” In addition to functionality, configurability, APIs, cloud architecture, security, data access, implementation, upgrades, scalability and total cost of ownership, I would ask: Does the platform support MCP or other open agent protocols? (Image credit: IIR.) For many years, when CIOs evaluated a new insurance core platform, one of the important questions we asked was: “Is the platform API-first?” There was a good reason for that.

item.title: AEGIS London and Augentic launch digital follow consortium
item.description: AEGIS London has partnered with tech-enabled MGA Augentic Underwriting to launch a cross-class digital follow consortium in the Lloyd’s market. The facility gives brokers access to follow capacity across AEGIS London’s open-market Property, Casualty and Specialty business through a single digital arrangement. Augentic uses algorithmic underwriting technology to help carriers deploy follow capacity within existing broker and carrier workflows without requiring portals or manual quoting.

item.title: Aegon CFO to step down
item.description: Aegon CFO Duncan Russell will step down and leave the company in April 2027 as the insurer prepares to move its head office and legal seat to the United States. Aegon has begun searching for Russell’s successor. Russell joined Aegon as CFO in 2020 after holding senior roles at Admiral Group and NN Group.

item.title: AXA UK adds fleet risk management partners
item.description: The partnerships will give AXA’s fleet customers access to additional risk management tools, resources, and industry expertise. Logistics UK provides training and fleet management services, including its Vision portal, which allows businesses to monitor drivers, vehicles, operator licensing, and other risk exposures in one place. The partnerships will support customers in developing fleet risk management strategies and adopting safer driving practices.

item.title: Insurify Expands ChatGPT Insurance Plugin
item.description: (Image source: Insurify.) Insurify (Cambridge, Mass.) has released an upgrade to its ChatGPT insurance comparison plugin, adding real-time personalized auto insurance quotes and in-chat shopping capabilities. “Insurance shopping behavior is changing, and the Insurify ChatGPT plugin can help consumers find the coverage they’re looking for by making ChatGPT a natural place for them to explore, compare, and act on their insurance needs all in one place.” Insurify says the upgrade builds on the first version of its ChatGPT plugin, formerly referred to as an app, which launched in February 2026. The Insurify ChatGPT insurance comparison plugin currently supports shoppers in Arizona, Kentucky, Ohio, Missouri, Nebraska, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Rhode Island, Utah, Vermont and Wisconsin.

Joe Brace, Operations Director, Lloyd’s Market Association and ACORD Board Member. “We are fortunate to have voices on the Board from across the global ACORD community, supporting our incoming CEO John Kellington and our colleagues as we shape a digital future for our industry together.” The appointments follow ACORD’s recent naming of John Kellington as CEO.

item.title: Carpe Launches Small Commercial Underwriting Engine
item.description: (Image credit: IIR.) Carpe (Santa Barbara, Calif.) has launched the Minerva Reasoning Engine, an AI-native underwriting solution for small commercial insurers. “We’ve spent more than a decade building exceptional commercial intelligence, and the Minerva Reasoning Engine gives carriers the reasoning they need to expand capacity while keeping underwriting judgment focused on the risks that deserve it.” Carpe positions Minerva as a response to challenges in small commercial underwriting, where carriers must balance the cost of researching a business against the potential profitability of the policy. Carpe says Minerva is available to commercial carriers seeking to increase underwriting capacity, improve decision consistency and grow small commercial books profitably.

item.title: Severity Gap Between Repairable BEVs and ICE Vehicles Reaches Record Low
item.description: The gap in average claims severity between repairable battery electric vehicles and internal combustion engine automobiles hit the lowest level on record in both the U.S. last quarter, with average repairable severity for BEVs at $5,684 compared with $4,955 for ICE vehicles. BEVs are still more costly to repair, but the data suggests “a combination of higher total loss frequency and a maturing electric vehicle fleet are bringing repair costs across powertrain types closer to parity.” Related: Report: Hybrid Vehicle Collision Claims Hit Record High in First Quarter The percentage of repairable claims involving BEVs was flat at 3% in the U.S., but mild hybrid electric vehicle (MHEV) claims reached a new high of 6%.

item.description: A new study suggests that some drivers feel that speeding is okay despite the risks, according to the AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety (AAAFTS). According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, speeding was a factor in nearly 30% of traffic fatalities in 2024. “Findings from this research show that some drivers in the United States view speeding as a normal part of driving,” said Dr.

item.title: Rates, Digital Support Boost Small Business Insurance Customer Satisfaction: JD Power
item.description: Small businesses’ overall satisfaction with small commercial insurers rose 15 points (to 713 on a 1,000-point scale), driven by improvements in digital support and rates, according to JD Power’s 2026 U.S. The biggest gains resulted from improved digital channels (+29 points), price for coverage (+16 points), problem resolution (+16 points) and product/coverage offerings (+16 points), according to the study which examines overall customer satisfaction among small commercial insurance customers with 50 or fewer employees. Erie Insurance ranked highest in customer satisfaction among small commercial insurers, with a score of 760.

item.title: History of Head Injury Could Affect Your Ability to Use Self-Driving Vehicles
item.description: “What this study brings into question is whether people will actually be willing and, more importantly, able to resume driving after long periods of disengagement.” Vehicles are classified on their self-driving ability on a range from 0-5 — with 0 being a vehicle completely driven by humans, and Level 5 being a vehicle that can drive itself under any circumstances without human interaction. Much of the appeal of self-driving vehicles is just that: the fact that they drive themselves. Still, there are times when a driver needs to put their hands on the wheel, and a new study from Binghamton University, State University of New York suggests that task could be more difficult if you have a history of head injuries.

item.title: Hannover Re Capital Partners build-out continues, looking to broaden investor base
item.description: Hannover Re is continuing to build-out its Bermuda-based insurance-linked securities (ILS) platform Hannover Re Capital Partners in 2026, with funds deployed for partnering investors already, the team being strengthened and a goal to onboard more investors while establishing new structures to support a range of investment opportunities. The global reinsurance firm launched its Hannover Re Capital Partners operation at the beginning of 2026 and in advance of that had explained the rationale as putting in place a missing piece of Hannover Re’s ILS offering . Earlier this year the company’s executives revealed that Hannover Re Capital Partners (HCP) started writing business at the January 1st 2026 reinsurance renewals .

item.title: Allstate’s pre-tax cat losses for current aggregate year reach $2.402bn after July
item.description: A busy July in catastrophe loss terms from severe weather activity has resulted in US insurer Allstate reporting $682 million in pre-tax losses, which has lifted the total across the current annual aggregate risk period for its catastrophe bonds to $2.402 billion so far. For July 2026, Allstate has reported $682 million of catastrophe losses for the month pre-tax, or $539 million after-tax. As a result, it’s impossible for us to know how much of July’s catastrophe losses have qualified under the terms of Allstate’s aggregate Sanders Re catastrophe bonds given the $50 million per-event deductible in-force within their coverage terms.

item.title: QBE promotes Jack Norman to Director of Financial Lines, International Markets
item.description: International business insurer QBE has appointed Jack Norman as Director of Financial Lines for its International Markets portfolio, based in London. In his new role, Norman reports to Kevin Shallow, Executive Director, International Markets, QBE. He will additionally join QBE’s International Markets leadership team and work closely with underwriting teams and product leaders to set the strategic direction for the financial lines portfolio.

item.title: Allstate estimates $682m in cat losses for July
item.description: The Allstate Corporation, a US personal property and casualty insurer, has estimated catastrophe losses of $682 million, or $539 million after tax, for July 2026. Allstate’s July estimate is an increase from June’s figure of $563 million , or $445 million after tax. Last month, Allstate also estimated total catastrophe losses for the second quarter of 2026 at $1.72 billion, or $1.36 billion after tax.

item.title: Vantage appoints Lucy Fato as General Counsel
item.description: (Vantage), a specialty re/insurance business, has appointed Lucy Fato as its new General Counsel as the company moves into its next phase following its acquisition by Howard Hughes Holdings. The change in leadership also follows the departure of Bobbi Anderson, who has stepped down as Vantage’s General Counsel. In her new position, Fato will become part of Vantage’s leadership team and will advise Marc Grandisson, the company’s Executive Chairman, on strategic matters.

item.title: Texas Homeowners, Industry Collide Over Transmission Lines
item.description: Flashes of yellow were all around the Texas Capitol grounds on Wednesday as legislators gathered to consider two of the most controversial issues in Texas politics: data centers and transmission lines. At the protest and nine-hour hearing that followed, lawmakers heard a variety of recommendations, including from local officials arguing for more local control of data center proposals and more time to reform the process behind approving transmission lines across Texas. The color — displayed on bandanas, pins, shirts and dresses — has become the symbol of a grassroots movement dedicated to blocking the buildout of 765-kilovolt transmission lines across the state.

item.title: Legacy Consolidator Marco Capital to Buy Insurance Services Firm Pro Global
item.description: Marco Capital, the property/casualty legacy consolidator and parent of insurance services group PoloWorks, has entered into an agreement to acquire Pro Global, subject to regulatory approval. The acquisition represents a significant milestone in its strategy to build an integrated legacy insurance and market-leading insurance services group – with an expanded global client offering and truly diversified income stream, Marco Capital said in a statement. “Polo Managing Agency is an early success story, and Marco continues to build PoloWorks into an even stronger, more ambitious, and well diversified insurance services business – an essential component of Marco Capital’s ecosystem,” Minshall added.

item.title: Romania Destroys Marine Drone Near Neptun Deep Gas Project: Minister
item.description: Romania scrambled F-16 fighter jets to destroy a marine drone spotted a few hundred meters from the Black Sea gas project Neptun Deep, Defence Minister Radu Miruta said on Thursday. Read more: Sweden Sees Russia Intensifying Cyber Attacks on Infrastructure Thursday’s incident follows similar action earlier this month when army divers destroyed two Gerbera-type drones drifting in the exclusive economic zone near the offshore Neptun Deep project. The incident underscores the growing threat to critical energy infrastructure in the Black Sea from drones and mines linked to Russia’s war in Ukraine, with Neptun Deep expected to make Romania the European Union’s largest gas producer when it comes onstream in 2027.

item.title: Ping An’s P&C business grows premium income 4% in first half of 2026
item.description: Ping An Insurance’s property and casualty business reported a 4% year-on-year increase in premium income in the first half of 2026, while a modest improvement in its combined operating ratio pointed to continued underwriting discipline. New energy vehicle insurance drives growth New energy vehicle insurance was one of the stronger areas of growth, with premium income increasing 21.5% year on year during the first half. During the first half, the P&C business issued 177,000 natural disaster early-warning alerts to approximately 120 million customers.

item.title: Tesla’s licensed carriers report Q2 2026 results
item.description: Tesla’s three licensed carriers reported their Q2 2026 financial results. Tesla Insurance Company, which offers coverage in California and Illinois, wrote $483.1 million in direct premiums in the first half of 2026, up 58% from $305.2 million a year earlier. Tesla Property & Casualty, which offers coverage in CO, MD, FL, MN, OH, TX, IN, TN, and UT, wrote $108.2 million in direct premiums in the first half of 2026, up 9% from $99 million a year earlier.

item.title: Stone Point Capital to acquire Ever.Ag’s risk management business
item.description: Agri-food technology company Ever.Ag announced that it has completed the sale of its risk management business to funds managed by Stone Point Capital. Stone Point brings the experience, resources, and long-term perspective to help us accelerate our strategy and continue delivering the comprehensive risk management solutions and market insights our customers and partners depend on.” – Pete Turk, co-founder and Executive Chairman of the Risk Management business. item.title: The Insurance Distribution Model of the Future

Zywave’s Eric Rentsch shares how AI is amplifying the role of insurance producers while reshaping brokerage operations, driving greater efficiency and organic growth. Let’s start with a clear picture of the role of an insurance producer and the client account management team.

item.title: A $100 Million Mall Reopening Is a Sign of LA’s Uneven Fire Recovery
item.description: At the community’s core, the luxury Palisades Village shopping center reopens Saturday after a $100 million restoration by billionaire developer Rick Caruso, marking a milestone in the area’s recovery. Nearby, wealthy homeowners and developers are rebuilding multimillion-dollar houses, and buyers are paying roughly $2 million for some burned-out lots. That lopsided recovery stands to reshape a 100-year-old community once known as “Mayberry by the Sea” for its small-town vibes.
